# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm gen:config-docs`; do not edit by hand. -->

The config source is chosen by `CAPYBARA_CONFIG_SOURCE` (`file` or `nacos`); environment variables win.
Nested keys use double underscores, e.g. `CAPYBARA_DB__URL` maps to `db.url`.
The defaults of secret fields do not appear in this document.

| Key | Env var | Type | Default | Hot | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db.url` | `CAPYBARA_DB__URL` | `string` | required | no | yes | PostgreSQL connection URL |
| `db.poolMax` | `CAPYBARA_DB__POOL_MAX` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Maximum PostgreSQL pool size |
| `db.connectTimeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_DB__CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `5000` | no | no | PostgreSQL connect timeout in milliseconds |
| `db.idleTimeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_DB__IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `60000` | no | no | How long an idle PostgreSQL connection stays in the pool, in milliseconds |
| `redis.url` | `CAPYBARA_REDIS__URL` | `string` | required | no | yes | Redis connection URL |
| `masterKey` | `CAPYBARA_MASTER_KEY` | `string` | required | no | yes | Base64 master key (32 bytes) for secret encryption |
| `masterKeyPrevious` | `CAPYBARA_MASTER_KEY_PREVIOUS` | `array<string>` | — | no | yes | Previous master keys kept during rotation |
| `extensions` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSIONS` | `array<string>` | `[]` | no | no | Extension names to load |
| `extensionConfig` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_CONFIG` | `record` | `{}` | no | no | Deployment-level config keyed by extension name |
| `extensionHost.dir` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__DIR` | `string` | `".capybara/plugins"` | no | no | Local directory where each replica unpacks installed extension packages (<dir>/<name>/<first 16 hex of sha256>/), relative to the working directory unless absolute (the image sets /var/lib/capybara/plugins); safe to wipe, replicas re-download from the package store |
| `extensionHost.drainSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__DRAIN_SECONDS` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Seconds in-flight tool calls and queue jobs of an extension being unloaded may keep running before they are aborted |
| `extensionHost.disposeTimeoutSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__DISPOSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Seconds an extension's dispose() may run when it is unloaded or replaced; after that the kernel logs a warning and moves on |
| `extensionHost.reloadSetupTimeoutSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__RELOAD_SETUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `number` | `60` | no | no | Seconds an extension's setup() may run when it is reloaded in a running process (enable, upgrade, dependency change), and when an installed extension (install record) is loaded at startup; on timeout the load fails and the previous instance, if any, stays. Built-in and config-declared extensions are not bounded at startup |
| `extensionHost.migrationTimeoutSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__MIGRATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `number` | `300` | no | no | Seconds an installed extension's migrations may run on the replica holding the migration lock; on timeout the migration session is terminated (statement_timeout bounds each statement, lock_timeout bounds lock waits), the lock is released and the replica reports migration_failed (retried on the next reconcile). Built-in and config-declared extensions are not bounded |
| `extensionHost.reconcileIntervalSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_HOST__RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `number` | `60` | no | no | Seconds between periodic reconciles of each replica's loaded extensions against the installed state in PostgreSQL |
| `packages.npmRegistry` | `CAPYBARA_PACKAGES__NPM_REGISTRY` | `string` | `"https://registry.npmjs.org"` | no | no | npm registry used to install extension packages by name |
| `packages.npmToken` | `CAPYBARA_PACKAGES__NPM_TOKEN` | `string` | optional | no | yes | Bearer token for the npm registry (private registries); sent only to the registry origin |
| `packages.maxBytes` | `CAPYBARA_PACKAGES__MAX_BYTES` | `number` | `52428800` | no | no | Largest extension package (.tgz) in bytes accepted by upload, npm install and the PostgreSQL package store. Lowering it also caps what replicas read back from the object store, so packages accepted earlier under a larger limit can no longer be synced. Uploads through the web tier (apps/web) are also capped by its own CAPYBARA_WEB_MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES (default 50 MiB); raise both together |
| `bootstrap.dir` | `CAPYBARA_BOOTSTRAP__DIR` | `string` | `"bootstrap"` | no | no | Offline directory for the bootstrap plugins, resolved against the working directory (/app/bootstrap in the image): a .tgz file here whose sha512 matches a pinned plugin is installed instead of downloading it from packages.npmRegistry |
| `catalog.staleInstallMinutes` | `CAPYBARA_CATALOG__STALE_INSTALL_MINUTES` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Minutes after which an organization plugin install still in the installing state (e.g. the replica crashed mid-install) may be cleaned up through uninstall, which rolls back the components it recorded |
| `marketplaces.official.enabled` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__OFFICIAL__ENABLED` | `boolean` | `true` | no | no | Use the official marketplace (the capybara-hq/plugins repository). Set to false for an offline deployment: while false it is never fetched (no requests, no refresh logs) and the admin UI shows offline mode |
| `marketplaces.official.url` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__OFFICIAL__URL` | `string` | `"https://github.com/capybara-hq/plugins.git"` | no | no | Address of the official marketplace (https): a git repository (a path ending in .git, read at its default branch from .capybara-plugin/marketplace.json) or a marketplace.json URL |
| `marketplaces.official.mirrors` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__OFFICIAL__MIRRORS` | `array<string>` | `[]` | no | no | Mirror URLs of the official marketplace's marketplace.json (https), tried in order when the main URL fails; only for a marketplace.json URL (a git marketplace has no mirrors: point url at a mirror repository instead) |
| `marketplaces.refreshIntervalMinutes` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES` | `number` | `360` | no | no | Minutes between periodic refreshes of every enabled marketplace (one run per period across all replicas) |
| `marketplaces.maxIndexBytes` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__MAX_INDEX_BYTES` | `number` | `5242880` | no | no | Largest marketplace.json in bytes; a larger response is rejected and the previous entries are kept |
| `marketplaces.allowInsecureLoopback` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK` | `boolean` | `false` | no | no | Testing only: allow plain http for marketplace and tarball URLs on loopback addresses |
| `marketplaces.allowPrivateHosts` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS` | `array<string>` | `[]` | no | no | Hosts or CIDRs that marketplace and git downloads may reach although they resolve to private addresses, e.g. an internal GitLab mirror. CIDR and IP entries match IP-literal hosts only; list internal DNS names as hostnames. Link-local addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fe80::/10) are always refused |
| `marketplaces.allowedHosts` | `CAPYBARA_MARKETPLACES__ALLOWED_HOSTS` | `array<string>` | `[]` | no | no | Hosts that marketplace entries may download git and archive sources from: hostnames or IP addresses (IPv6 without brackets), without scheme or port, compared case-insensitively with the URL's hostname. Empty means unrestricted; an entry on another host is listed as not importable and its import is refused |
| `net.httpsProxy` | `CAPYBARA_NET__HTTPS_PROXY` | `string` | optional | no | yes | HTTP(S) egress proxy for marketplace, archive and git downloads, e.g. http://user:password@proxy.internal:3128. https downloads tunnel through it with CONNECT and the kernel no longer resolves their hosts: the proxy does, so blocking private and internal addresses becomes the proxy's job (IP-literal URLs are still checked against marketplaces.allowPrivateHosts). Loopback hosts never use it. Credentials in the URL are sent as Basic Proxy-Authorization and never logged |
| `net.noProxy` | `CAPYBARA_NET__NO_PROXY` | `array<string>` | `[]` | no | no | Hostnames or IP addresses that bypass net.httpsProxy (an entry also matches its subdomains; a leading dot is allowed). These hosts are resolved locally and must resolve to public addresses unless listed in marketplaces.allowPrivateHosts |
| `extensionPermissions.autoApprove` | `CAPYBARA_EXTENSION_PERMISSIONS__AUTO_APPROVE` | `boolean` | `false` | no | no | Approve extension permissions automatically at startup (development and trials only). When false, an extension that is new or whose upgrade asks for more permissions is not loaded until an admin runs `capybara extensions approve <name>` |
| `http.port` | `CAPYBARA_HTTP__PORT` | `number` | `8080` | no | no | HTTP listen port |
| `http.trustProxy` | `CAPYBARA_HTTP__TRUST_PROXY` | `boolean \| number \| array<string>` | `false` | no | no | Which X-Forwarded-For hops to trust for the client IP (login rate limiting, session records): false (use the socket address), a hop count, or a list of trusted proxy IPs/CIDRs (recommended; a JSON array or a comma-separated string; a /0 prefix is refused). true trusts any client-supplied X-Forwarded-For and lets clients spoof their IP. A hop count is only safe when the service is reachable solely through exactly that many proxies |
| `http.replicaId` | `CAPYBARA_HTTP__REPLICA_ID` | `string \| number` | optional | no | no | Optional replica identifier; when set, every HTTP response carries an x-capybara-replica header with this value (used by the dual-replica test harness and for debugging load balancers) |
| `http.swagger` | `CAPYBARA_HTTP__SWAGGER` | `boolean` | `false` | no | no | Serve the OpenAPI document and swagger UI at /docs (JSON at /docs-json). The routes are not authenticated, so enable it in development and trials only |
| `http.publicUrl` | `CAPYBARA_HTTP__PUBLIC_URL` | `string` | optional | no | no | Externally reachable origin of the web app (apps/web, which proxies /api to the kernel), not the kernel's own address; required for OAuth connectors: the redirect URI is <publicUrl>/api/v1/oauth/callback (served through the web /api proxy, which also carries the OAuth binding cookie) and the callback redirects to web pages under it, e.g. https://capybara.example.com |
| `roles` | `CAPYBARA_ROLES` | `array<"api" \| "worker" \| "gateway">` | `["api","worker","gateway"]` | no | no | Roles this process runs: a JSON array or a comma-separated string, e.g. ["api"] or api,worker |
| `auth.accessTokenTtlSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | `number` | `900` | no | no | Lifetime of web session access tokens in seconds |
| `auth.refreshTokenTtlDays` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Absolute lifetime of a web session (refresh token) in days; refreshing does not extend it |
| `auth.cookieSecure` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__COOKIE_SECURE` | `boolean` | `true` | no | no | Set the Secure attribute on session cookies; set false only for local trials over plain http |
| `auth.setupToken` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__SETUP_TOKEN` | `string` | optional | no | yes | If set, the setup wizard requires this token |
| `auth.loginSources` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__LOGIN_SOURCES` | `array<string>` | `[]` | yes | no | Extension names (providing identity-source@1) offered as third-party sign-in on the login page, in this order; the sign-in callback URL is <http.publicUrl>/api/v1/auth/sso/<plugin>/callback |
| `auth.trustedIdentitySources` | `CAPYBARA_AUTH__TRUSTED_IDENTITY_SOURCES` | `array<string>` | `[]` | yes | no | Identity source keys "<plugin>:<tenantId>" (one tenant each, e.g. "lark:tenant_1") whose external identities are trusted: on third-party sign-in, when the identity's email and an existing account's email are both verified and equal, the identity is linked to that account instead of creating a new one; and accounts created through a trusted source count as email-verified. Only list tenants (workspaces / apps) that your enterprise controls; otherwise anyone in that tenant could claim your users' emails. Entries without a tenant id are rejected |
| `runtime.maxSteps` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__MAX_STEPS` | `number` | `50` | no | no | Maximum model steps per agent run before the final wrap-up |
| `runtime.wakeOnBackgroundTask` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__WAKE_ON_BACKGROUND_TASK` | `boolean` | `true` | no | no | Whether the finish of a background Bash task or a sub-agent's delivery starts a run on an idle conversation or sub-agent (the person who started the task's or the sub-agent's run is the trigger); an organization can override it in its settings. When false the event is only logged and shown, and the next message picks it up |
| `runtime.maxRunSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__MAX_RUN_SECONDS` | `number` | `900` | no | no | Maximum wall-clock duration of one agent run in seconds (time spent waiting for people is not counted). Sandbox commands are limited to the time left in the run, so agents that need long commands need maxRunSeconds >= sandbox.limits.maxCommandSeconds |
| `runtime.streamIdleMs` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__STREAM_IDLE_MS` | `number` | `60000` | no | no | Default model stream idle watchdog in milliseconds (a model's own streamIdleTimeoutMs takes precedence) |
| `runtime.maxOutputTokens` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `number` | `16000` | no | no | Default output-token limit per model call when the agent does not set maxOutputTokens (an agent's maxOutputTokens overrides it; either is capped by the model's own maximum) |
| `runtime.compactionThreshold` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__COMPACTION_THRESHOLD` | `number` | `0.8` | no | no | Compact the conversation when the estimated input reaches this fraction of the context window |
| `runtime.keepRecentTurns` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__KEEP_RECENT_TURNS` | `number` | `4` | no | no | Number of recent user turns kept verbatim when compacting |
| `runtime.workerConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Maximum agent runs executed concurrently by one worker process |
| `runtime.orgConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__ORG_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `10` | yes | no | Maximum agent runs executing concurrently per organization across all replicas |
| `runtime.jobLockMs` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__JOB_LOCK_MS` | `number` | `30000` | no | no | Lock duration of an agent run job in milliseconds (BullMQ lockDuration), also the TTL of the conversation run lock; a run whose worker stops renewing them is considered stalled after this long and resumes on another worker |
| `runtime.stalledIntervalMs` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__STALLED_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `30000` | no | no | How often workers check for stalled agent run jobs in milliseconds (BullMQ stalledInterval) |
| `runtime.sseHeartbeatMs` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__SSE_HEARTBEAT_MS` | `number` | `15000` | no | no | Interval in milliseconds between heartbeat comments on a conversation event stream (SSE) |
| `runtime.sseRecheckMs` | `CAPYBARA_RUNTIME__SSE_RECHECK_MS` | `number` | `60000` | no | no | How often an open conversation event stream (SSE) re-checks that the viewer may still access the conversation, in milliseconds; the stream closes when access is lost |
| `tools.timeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `60000` | no | no | Timeout of one tool call in milliseconds |
| `tools.breakerFailures` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__BREAKER_FAILURES` | `number` | `5` | no | no | Consecutive failures of one connector that open its circuit breaker |
| `tools.breakerOpenSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__BREAKER_OPEN_SECONDS` | `number` | `60` | no | no | Seconds an open circuit breaker rejects calls before allowing a probe |
| `tools.outputSpillChars` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__OUTPUT_SPILL_CHARS` | `number` | `50000` | no | no | Tool results longer than this many characters are archived and replaced by a preview |
| `tools.outputPreviewChars` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__OUTPUT_PREVIEW_CHARS` | `number` | `2000` | no | no | Characters of an archived tool result kept in the conversation as a preview |
| `tools.outputRetentionDays` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__OUTPUT_RETENTION_DAYS` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Days archived tool outputs are kept before cleanup |
| `tools.approvalTimeoutHours` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_HOURS` | `number` | `24` | no | no | Hours a pending approval or question waits before it expires (treated as denied) |
| `tools.searchThresholdTools` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__SEARCH_THRESHOLD_TOOLS` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Switch to on-demand tool search when an agent has more than this many tools |
| `tools.searchThresholdTokens` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__SEARCH_THRESHOLD_TOKENS` | `number` | `8000` | no | no | Switch to on-demand tool search when tool definitions exceed this many estimated tokens |
| `tools.driftIntervalHours` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__DRIFT_INTERVAL_HOURS` | `number` | `24` | no | no | Hours between checks of connectors for changed tool definitions |
| `tools.maxResultReadChars` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__MAX_RESULT_READ_CHARS` | `number` | `20000` | no | no | Maximum characters returned by one ReadToolOutput call |
| `tools.oauthAllowInsecureLoopback` | `CAPYBARA_TOOLS__OAUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOOPBACK` | `boolean` | `false` | no | no | Allow OAuth discovery, registration and token endpoints over plain http on loopback hosts (development and tests only; production requires https) |
| `channels.leaseTtlMs` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__LEASE_TTL_MS` | `number` | `30000` | no | no | TTL of the lease that lets one gateway replica hold a channel connection's long connection, in milliseconds; another replica takes over after the holder stops renewing it for this long |
| `channels.scanIntervalMs` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__SCAN_INTERVAL_MS` | `number` | `10000` | no | no | How often each gateway replica renews its channel leases and scans for active channel connections that nobody holds, in milliseconds |
| `channels.shareSlack` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__SHARE_SLACK` | `number` | `1` | no | no | Extra channel long connections a gateway replica may hold above its fair share (connections divided by live gateway replicas); a replica above share + slack hands one back per scan round |
| `channels.retryBaseMs` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__RETRY_BASE_MS` | `number` | `5000` | no | no | First retry delay after a channel long connection fails, in milliseconds; doubles on each consecutive failure up to 5 minutes |
| `channels.deliveryConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__DELIVERY_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `100` | no | no | How many channel outbound delivery jobs one worker replica runs at the same time (each job follows one conversation while its run streams output) |
| `channels.deliveryIdleMs` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__DELIVERY_IDLE_MS` | `number` | `15000` | no | no | A channel delivery job that has caught up ends after this many milliseconds without new conversation output; the next event of the conversation starts a new job |
| `channels.webhookBaseUrl` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__WEBHOOK_BASE_URL` | `string` | optional | no | no | Public origin (https) that reaches the gateway replicas, e.g. https://im.example.com; a channel connection's webhook callback URL is <webhookBaseUrl>/channels/webhook/<connection id>. Without it connections cannot switch to webhook inbound (long connections stay the default). Plain http is accepted only for loopback hosts when tools.oauthAllowInsecureLoopback is true (tests) |
| `channels.webhookMaxBodyBytes` | `CAPYBARA_CHANNELS__WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | `number` | `1048576` | no | no | Largest channel webhook request body in bytes; a larger request is rejected with 413 |
| `storage.purgeDeletedOrgsAfterDays` | `CAPYBARA_STORAGE__PURGE_DELETED_ORGS_AFTER_DAYS` | `number` | `30` | no | no | Days after an organization is deleted before a maintenance job permanently deletes its objects from object storage (kernel/<orgId>/ and plugins/*/<orgId>/) |
| `attachments.maxBytes` | `CAPYBARA_ATTACHMENTS__MAX_BYTES` | `number` | `20971520` | no | no | Maximum size in bytes of one chat attachment (images are also capped at 5 MiB, the model input limit) |
| `attachments.allowedTypes` | `CAPYBARA_ATTACHMENTS__ALLOWED_TYPES` | `array<"image/png" \| "image/jpeg" \| "image/gif" \| "image/webp" \| "application/pdf" \| "text/plain" \| "text/markdown" \| "text/csv">` | `["image/png","image/jpeg","image/gif","image/webp","application/pdf","text/plain","text/markdown","text/csv"]` | no | no | Content types accepted for chat attachments |
| `attachments.maxPerMessage` | `CAPYBARA_ATTACHMENTS__MAX_PER_MESSAGE` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Maximum number of attachments in one message |
| `attachments.unboundTtlHours` | `CAPYBARA_ATTACHMENTS__UNBOUND_TTL_HOURS` | `number` | `24` | no | no | Hours after upload before an attachment never used in a message is deleted (row and object) |
| `attachments.requestMediaBytes` | `CAPYBARA_ATTACHMENTS__REQUEST_MEDIA_BYTES` | `number` | `20971520` | no | no | Budget of raw attachment bytes in one model request; the newest attachments are kept and older ones are replaced with a placeholder. At most 24 MiB: base64 inflates it by about 4/3, and common providers cap a request at 32 MB |
| `subagents.maxDepth` | `CAPYBARA_SUBAGENTS__MAX_DEPTH` | `number` | `3` | yes | no | Levels of sub-agents below the conversation's own agent; 1 means sub-agents cannot dispatch sub-agents of their own. Organizations can be given their own value in the deployment setting subagentLimitOverrides |
| `subagents.maxConcurrentPerConversation` | `CAPYBARA_SUBAGENTS__MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_CONVERSATION` | `number` | `4` | yes | no | Sub-agents one conversation may have running at the same time, whichever of its runs dispatched them; agent calls beyond it are refused. Organizations can be given their own value in subagentLimitOverrides |
| `subagents.maxDispatchesPerRun` | `CAPYBARA_SUBAGENTS__MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_RUN` | `number` | `50` | yes | no | Sub-agents the whole tree under a person's message may dispatch in total, counted across every level (nested dispatches and SendMessage messages that restart an idle sub-agent included); later agent calls and such messages are refused. 0 means no limit. Organizations can be given their own value in subagentLimitOverrides |
| `subagents.maxTokensPerRun` | `CAPYBARA_SUBAGENTS__MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN` | `number` | `5000000` | yes | no | Tokens (input, output and cache) all sub-agents of the tree under a person's message may use together; at the cap running sub-agents stop and new dispatches are refused. 0 means no limit; otherwise at least 10,000. Organizations can be given their own value in subagentLimitOverrides |
| `web.search.maxResults` | `CAPYBARA_WEB__SEARCH__MAX_RESULTS` | `number` | `10` | yes | no | Maximum number of results one WebSearch call returns to the model, however many the search provider returns |
| `web.fetch.maxPageChars` | `CAPYBARA_WEB__FETCH__MAX_PAGE_CHARS` | `number` | `400000` | yes | no | Maximum characters of a fetched page kept for answering a WebFetch prompt; longer pages are truncated |
| `web.fetch.maxAnswerTokens` | `CAPYBARA_WEB__FETCH__MAX_ANSWER_TOKENS` | `number` | `4000` | yes | no | Maximum output tokens of the model call that answers a WebFetch prompt from the page |
| `web.fetch.cacheSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_WEB__FETCH__CACHE_SECONDS` | `number` | `900` | yes | no | Seconds a fetched page is cached per organization and URL; 0 turns the cache off |
| `web.fetch.timeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_WEB__FETCH__TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `180000` | yes | no | Time limit of one WebFetch call in milliseconds, the provider's fetch and the answering model call together; replaces tools.timeoutMs for WebFetch |
| `sandbox.image` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__IMAGE` | `string` | optional | no | no | Image for environment instances, passed to the sandbox extension; unset (the default), each extension uses the image published with its own version (ghcr.io/capybara-hq/capybara-sandbox). Set it to a locally built or mirrored image for offline deployments; an extension that builds instances from its own template may ignore it |
| `sandbox.lockWaitSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS` | `number` | `75` | no | no | Seconds a sandbox call waits for the environment's instance (while it is being created, resumed or suspended, or all its concurrent command slots are taken) before failing with sandbox.busy; keep it above the 60-second sandbox lock TTL so a call after a replica crash waits for the dead replica's lock to expire |
| `sandbox.maxConcurrentCommands` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__MAX_CONCURRENT_COMMANDS` | `number` | `6` | yes | no | Sandbox commands and file operations that may run at the same time in one environment, shared by all its conversations and their sub-agents; 1 runs them one at a time |
| `sandbox.deliverMaxBytes` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__DELIVER_MAX_BYTES` | `number` | `104857600` | no | no | Largest file in bytes an agent may deliver from its sandbox to the user as an artifact (Deliver) |
| `sandbox.background.maxTasks` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__BACKGROUND__MAX_TASKS` | `number` | `4` | no | no | Most background Bash tasks (run_in_background) that may run at once in one conversation, its sub-agents included (counted per root conversation, not per environment); a launch beyond it is refused |
| `sandbox.background.maxSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__BACKGROUND__MAX_SECONDS` | `number` | `7200` | no | no | Longest a background Bash task may run, in seconds; the task is killed at its deadline and ends as timed_out. Clamped to sandbox.limits.maxCommandSeconds; not limited by runtime.maxRunSeconds |
| `sandbox.background.pollSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__BACKGROUND__POLL_SECONDS` | `number` | `10` | no | no | How often the worker checks the running background Bash tasks of every environment for a finish, in seconds; read when the worker starts |
| `sandbox.limits.cpu` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__CPU` | `number` | `1` | no | no | CPU cores for each environment instance; applies to instances created after the change (an extension that sizes instances by its own template, such as E2B, may not apply it) |
| `sandbox.limits.memoryMb` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__MEMORY_MB` | `number` | `2048` | no | no | Memory limit of each environment instance in MiB; applies to instances created after the change (an extension that sizes instances by its own template, such as E2B, may not apply it) |
| `sandbox.limits.diskMb` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__DISK_MB` | `number` | `5120` | no | no | Disk limit of each environment's file system in MiB; applies to file systems created after the change (Docker: only with a volume driver that supports size; an extension whose storage cannot be sized may not apply it) |
| `sandbox.limits.maxCommandSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__MAX_COMMAND_SECONDS` | `number` | `7200` | no | no | Longest a single sandbox command may run, in seconds. A command also stops when its run is about to reach runtime.maxRunSeconds, so long commands need runtime.maxRunSeconds >= maxCommandSeconds (a startup warning is logged otherwise) |
| `sandbox.limits.suspendAfterIdleMinutes` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__SUSPEND_AFTER_IDLE_MINUTES` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Minutes without a command from any conversation of the environment before its running instance is suspended (files are kept, processes end) |
| `sandbox.limits.destroyAfterInactiveDays` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__DESTROY_AFTER_INACTIVE_DAYS` | `number` | `7` | no | no | Days without use before an environment's instance is destroyed; its files are kept until the environment is deleted, and the next use starts a new instance on them |
| `sandbox.limits.maxRunningMinutes` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__MAX_RUNNING_MINUTES` | `number` | `120` | no | no | Minutes an environment's instance may run continuously before it is suspended even while in use (skipped while a command is running) |
| `sandbox.limits.egress` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__EGRESS` | `"none" \| "allowlist" \| "open"` | `"allowlist"` | no | no | Outbound network from environment instances: none, allowlist (only allowHosts) or open; applies to instances created after the change, existing ones keep theirs until destroyed |
| `sandbox.limits.allowHosts` | `CAPYBARA_SANDBOX__LIMITS__ALLOW_HOSTS` | `array<string>` | `["registry.npmjs.org","pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","github.com","codeload.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","release-assets.githubusercontent.com"]` | no | no | Hosts environment instances may reach when egress is allowlist: lowercase hostnames, optional leading '*.', no IPs, ports or internal-only names; applies to instances created after the change |
| `environments.maxPersonal` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__MAX_PERSONAL` | `number` | `10` | yes | no | Most personal environments a member may have in one org, the default one included; creating one more fails with environment.limit_reached |
| `environments.device.reconnectGraceSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__DEVICE__RECONNECT_GRACE_SECONDS` | `number` | `120` | yes | no | Seconds a connected machine may stay disconnected before its environment is reported offline; also sent to the device program at sign-in |
| `environments.device.leaseTtlMs` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__DEVICE__LEASE_TTL_MS` | `number` | `30000` | no | no | Milliseconds the replica holding a machine's connection keeps its lease without renewing it; at least 6000 |
| `environments.device.authCodeTtlSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__DEVICE__AUTH_CODE_TTL_SECONDS` | `number` | `600` | no | no | Seconds a device sign-in code stays valid before the program must start over (device.expired) |
| `environments.device.pollIntervalSeconds` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__DEVICE__POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | `number` | `5` | no | no | Seconds the device program waits between token polls during sign-in; polling faster gets device.slow_down |
| `environments.device.maxFrameBytes` | `CAPYBARA_ENVIRONMENTS__DEVICE__MAX_FRAME_BYTES` | `number` | `16777216` | no | no | Largest WebSocket frame in bytes accepted from or sent to a connected machine |
| `evals.orgConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__ORG_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `2` | yes | no | Maximum eval cases executing concurrently per organization across all replicas |
| `evals.workerConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `4` | no | no | Eval case jobs one replica processes at the same time |
| `evals.defaultTokenCap` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__DEFAULT_TOKEN_CAP` | `number` | `1000000` | no | no | Token cap of an eval run when none is given; the run stops sending new model requests once it is reached |
| `evals.maxTokenCap` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__MAX_TOKEN_CAP` | `number` | `20000000` | no | no | Largest token cap an eval run may ask for |
| `evals.maxCasesPerSet` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__MAX_CASES_PER_SET` | `number` | `500` | no | no | Maximum number of cases in one eval set |
| `evals.maxCaseBytes` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__MAX_CASE_BYTES` | `number` | `4194304` | no | no | Largest log snapshot in bytes (serialized JSON) one eval case may store; larger runs cannot be added |
| `evals.judgeMaxOutputTokens` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__JUDGE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | `number` | `1024` | no | no | Maximum output tokens of one LLM judge request |
| `evals.maxConsecutiveErrors` | `CAPYBARA_EVALS__MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS` | `number` | `10` | no | no | Consecutive failed results after which an eval run is marked failed and its remaining cases are skipped |
| `models.listTimeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_MODELS__LIST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `10000` | yes | no | Time limit in milliseconds for one model provider's model list (listModels, which may page through a large platform catalog); a provider that exceeds it is treated as failing to list |
| `models.embedTimeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_MODELS__EMBED_TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `60000` | yes | no | Time limit in milliseconds for one embed call to a model provider (one batch of an extension's ctx.models.embed); the call is aborted and fails with a timeout model error |
| `hooks.timeoutMs` | `CAPYBARA_HOOKS__TIMEOUT_MS` | `number` | `5000` | yes | no | Time limit in milliseconds for one extension hook call; a policy hook that exceeds it denies the call, an observe hook is skipped |
| `hooks.usageReportConcurrency` | `CAPYBARA_HOOKS__USAGE_REPORT_CONCURRENCY` | `number` | `16` | no | no | usage.report delivery jobs one worker replica processes at the same time |
| `hooks.usageReportKeepHours` | `CAPYBARA_HOOKS__USAGE_REPORT_KEEP_HOURS` | `number` | `24` | no | no | Hours a finished usage.report job is kept in Redis so re-enqueueing the same usage event (resumed step, sweeper) is deduplicated; at least 1, well above the sweeper's 10-minute overlap |
| `log.level` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__LEVEL` | `"debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error"` | `"info"` | yes | no | Log level |
| `log.format` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__FORMAT` | `"auto" \| "pretty" \| "json"` | `"auto"` | no | no | Console log format: pretty (one readable line per record, colored on a terminal), json (one JSON line per record) or auto (pretty when stdout is a terminal, else json, so containers log JSON) |
| `log.loki.url` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__LOKI__URL` | `string` | optional | no | no | Loki base URL (e.g. http://loki:3100) or its full push URL; when set, every log record is also pushed there (batched, JSON lines). Unset: nothing is sent |
| `log.loki.username` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__LOKI__USERNAME` | `string` | optional | no | no | Loki basic auth user name |
| `log.loki.password` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__LOKI__PASSWORD` | `string` | optional | no | yes | Loki basic auth password |
| `log.loki.labels` | `CAPYBARA_LOG__LOKI__LABELS` | `record` | `{}` | no | no | Extra Loki stream labels, e.g. {"env":"prod"}; every stream also has job (capybara unless set here), role (the process's roles) and level |

## Nacos config source

With `CAPYBARA_CONFIG_SOURCE=nacos`, Nacos is specified by the following environment variables (they are not config keys and cannot be written in the config file):

| Env var | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `CAPYBARA_NACOS_SERVER` | Nacos address (e.g. `nacos:8848`; the protocol defaults to http). Required |
| `CAPYBARA_NACOS_NAMESPACE` | Namespace ID. Required |
| `CAPYBARA_NACOS_DATA_ID` | The config's dataId (YAML). Required; the group is fixed to `DEFAULT_GROUP` |
| `CAPYBARA_NACOS_USERNAME` / `CAPYBARA_NACOS_PASSWORD` | Username and password when Nacos has authentication on: the kernel logs in to obtain an accessToken and logs in again after 80% of `tokenTtl` or on a 403; set both or neither |
| `CAPYBARA_NACOS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | An accessToken used as is (the login endpoint is not called); cannot be set together with the username and password |

## Web tier (apps/web) environment variables

The web tier is a separate process (started through `apps/web/server.mjs`); it does not read the kernel config and only honors the following environment variables:

| Env var | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `CAPYBARA_KERNEL_URL` | The kernel address that the `/api/*` proxy forwards to; default `http://localhost:8080` |
| `PORT` / `CAPYBARA_WEB_HOST` | The web tier's listen port (default 3000) and address |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_TRUST_PROXY` | Proxies in front of the web tier (TLS proxy, load balancer) trusted to report the client address in `X-Forwarded-For`: a hop count (`1` = the nearest proxy) or a list of IPs / CIDRs, comma-separated or a JSON array, in the grammar of `http.trustProxy` (dotted netmasks, `loopback` / `linklocal` / `uniquelocal`; a range that trusts every address such as `/0` is refused; no `true` / `false`). Unset (default) trusts nothing: the socket peer is the client, so behind a proxy every user shares the proxy's address for login rate limiting. A hop count is only safe when the web tier is reachable solely through exactly that many proxies. Either way the kernel receives one sanitized client address; a malformed value stops the web tier at startup |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS` | Production only: after SIGTERM / SIGINT, how long in-flight requests (including SSE streams) may run before the process exits; default 5000 |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS` | How long an idle HTTP keep-alive connection to the web tier stays open, in milliseconds; default 65000. Keep it above the idle timeout of any load balancer or proxy in front of the web tier (often 60 s): otherwise the web tier may close a connection just as the proxy reuses it, and that request fails (a 502 at the proxy). A value that is not a positive integer stops the web tier at startup |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_MAX_BODY_BYTES` | Request body limit of the `/api/*` proxy, default 1 MiB (matches the kernel's bodyLimit) |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES` | Request body limit for extension package and plugin uploads (`/api/v1/admin/extensions/packages/file`, `/api/v1/admin/catalog/import/file`, `/api/v1/orgs/:orgId/catalog/uploads/file`), default 50 MiB, forwarded while being read. This is the web tier's limit; the kernel additionally rejects by `packages.maxBytes`. Raise both together, otherwise a large package uploaded through the web is first rejected by the web tier with a 413 |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_OBJECT_STORE_URL` | Object storage on the web origin: the object store's address as web reaches it (e.g. `http://seaweedfs-s3:8333`). When set, web proxies `/<bucket>/**` (and `/<bucket>` itself for POST only) there, so browsers upload attachments (presigned POST) and download attachments and artifacts (presigned GET) through web; set the object-store extension's `publicEndpoint` to the web origin with `forcePathStyle: true`. Only GET, HEAD and POST; the path is forwarded unchanged; cookies and authorization are not forwarded; responses carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`; uploads are capped at `CAPYBARA_WEB_MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES`. Unset (default): off |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_OBJECT_STORE_BUCKET` | With `CAPYBARA_WEB_OBJECT_STORE_URL`: the bucket, equal to the object-store extension's `bucket` (it is the first path segment web proxies) |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_OBJECT_STORE_PUBLIC_HOST` | With `CAPYBARA_WEB_OBJECT_STORE_URL`: the host of the extension's `publicEndpoint` (a host such as `capybara.example.com`, or that URL). Sent upstream as `Host` instead of the incoming one, because presigned URLs sign the host they were issued for and front proxies rewrite it |
| `CAPYBARA_WEB_GATEWAY_URL` | Connected machines on the web origin: a `gateway` replica's address as web reaches it (an http(s) URL, e.g. `http://gateway:8080`). WebSocket upgrades on exactly `/device/connect` are forwarded to it (`capybara-device` connects at `<http.publicUrl>/device/connect`). Unset, they go to `CAPYBARA_KERNEL_URL` (the kernel runs every role unless the deployment splits them), so only deployments with separate gateway replicas set it (compose does). A malformed value stops the web tier at startup |
| `CAPYBARA_DEV_UI` | When set to `1`, production builds also serve the `/dev/ui` component catalog page (off by default) |
